problem:
Consider the curve defined parametrically as 

$$
x=2\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,y=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,t\in [0,\pi ].
$$

What integral gives the surface area generated when this curve is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis?

activity_context.topic_title: Surface Areas of Revolution for Parametric Curves

feedback.problem:
Consider the curve defined parametrically as 

$$
x=\operatorname{cosh}⁡t,\,y=\operatorname{cosh}⁡2t,\,t\in [0,2].
$$

What integral gives the surface area generated when this curve is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis?
feedback.worked_solution:
We can find the surface area generated when a curve is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis using the formula

$$
S=\int 2\pi x\,\text{d}s.
$$

Since our curve is given in parametric form, we have

$$
\text{d}s=\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

Therefore, we will use

$$
S=2\pi {\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}x\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t.
$$

We are told that the limits of integration are from ${t}_{1}=0$ to ${t}_{2}=2.$ 

Computing the derivatives, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cosh}⁡t)=\operatorname{sinh}⁡t \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cosh}⁡2t)=2\operatorname{sinh}⁡2t.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =2\pi {\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}x\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}\operatorname{cosh}⁡t\sqrt{{(\operatorname{sinh}⁡t)}^{2}+{(2\operatorname{sinh}⁡2t)}^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}\operatorname{cosh}⁡t\sqrt{{sinh}^{2}⁡t+4{sinh}^{2}⁡2t}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the identity $\operatorname{sinh}⁡2t=2\operatorname{sinh}⁡t\operatorname{cosh}⁡t,$ we can rewrite our integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}\operatorname{cosh}⁡t\sqrt{{sinh}^{2}⁡t+4{sinh}^{2}⁡2t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}\operatorname{cosh}⁡t\sqrt{{sinh}^{2}⁡t+4(2\operatorname{sinh}⁡t\operatorname{cosh}⁡t)^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}\operatorname{cosh}⁡t\sqrt{{sinh}^{2}⁡t+16{sinh}^{2}⁡t{cosh}^{2}⁡t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}\operatorname{cosh}⁡t\sqrt{{sinh}^{2}⁡t(1+16{cosh}^{2}⁡t)}\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}\operatorname{cosh}⁡t\cdot \sqrt{{sinh}^{2}⁡t}\cdot \sqrt{1+16{cosh}^{2}⁡t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}\operatorname{cosh}⁡t\cdot |\operatorname{sinh}⁡t|\cdot \sqrt{1+16{cosh}^{2}⁡t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}\operatorname{sinh}⁡t\operatorname{cosh}⁡t\sqrt{1+16{cosh}^{2}⁡t}\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$
